answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity capital bond that is slashed, not just staked. Every new agent must lock a fixed minimum before its work is counted, and each extra identity needs its own full lock. Because payouts per epoch are capped, spinning up N fake agents costs N times the bond while the reward pool stays flat, so marginal return turns negative fast. A trusted vertex in the reputation graph also has to co-sign new joiners; duplicate keys must beacon the same collateral and fail, leaving each attacker paying the bond and losing it on detection, with no cheap sable cover.
